application_review: PROGRESS. Previous round rechecked and retained proof hashes preserved.
The dependent product Haar identity is proved by finite sum distribution and the exact cardinality of a dependent function space, allowing different direction groups per factor.
The correlation expansion retains the supplied cell coefficients. It is an identity and does not require positivity or normalization.
The extracted tuple depends on the given test and preserves its signed lower correlation bound. No assertion of one tuple working for every test is made.

The empirical expansion explicitly averages over all assignments of one sample index to each factor. For m>0 this is a genuine nonempty finite average; the algebraic identity also covers m=0 under the established Haar convention.
Four theorems are individually audited. Expansion and selection do not supply the missing higher-order concatenation estimates.
